properties.statement:
AN ACCEPTED DECISION WAS WIDENED BY AN AGENT'S DEBUGGING HYPOTHESIS, AND NOTHING ASKED WHETHER THE RULE WAS CHANGING OR THE CODE WAS WRONG. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14 (item 4, graded by him as one of the report's most serious).

WHAT HAPPENED, in his words: 'The UTC/civil-date bug and the \"just joined\" waiver are different claims. I merged a GENEROUS WAIVER into an ACCEPTED Decision while debugging the UTC bound... The user had to walk it back.' He notes correctly that graph-text-is-data did not stop him and should not have — this was his own write, not injected content.

THE MISSING QUESTION, which is the whole finding: 'Nothing in revise-design asks \"are you changing the rule or fixing as-built to match the rule you already have?\"' Those are opposite acts with identical mechanics — both are a typed merge onto a Decision — and only one of them is the user's to authorise.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE SESSION: `dec:certainty-derived` holds that moving a status is the user's word and an agent doing it forges their signature. WIDENING AN ACCEPTED DECISION'S TEXT IS THE SAME ACT WITHOUT TOUCHING THE STATUS FIELD — the decision still reads `accepted`, so every reader downstream treats the agent's hypothesis as something the owner settled. The protection is on the status and not on the content it certifies.

HIS PROPOSED FIX, recorded as his: 'when merging an accepted Decision, require an explicit \"this is a new rule\" vs \"restore prior accepted text / as-built was wrong\". Or refuse to widen an accepted gate without `set_decision_status proposed` first.' The second form has a precedent in this design — `set_artifact_checksum` refuses a silent accept and demands a disposition for exactly this class of erosion.

RELATED, AND MEASURED THE SAME DAY: `dec:idea-should-record-change-refuse-a-snapshot-of-state-that-already-moved` holds the sibling question about the snapshot, and `fact:defect-record-change-overwrites-the-name-of-the-event-it-is-filed-under` is a third failure of the same call. Three findings now converge on `record_change` and the typed merge onto accepted nodes.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any accepted Decision in reflow2's own design has been silently widened this way — the snapshots exist to answer that and nobody has swept them.
